questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Burundi?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Burundi on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Burundi article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Rwanda to the north, Tanzania to the east and south and the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Burundi?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Burundi is the Burundian franc.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Burundi on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Burundi on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Burundi about 27,834 square kilometres; Eswatini about 17,364 square kilometres; Mauritius about 2,040 square kilometres; Seychelles about 459 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Gitega?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Burundi is Gitega.
